headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.few}: it is the only configuration of {n_candidates|int} that clears every gate, though it clears overall accuracy by just {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points.
lede: Every configuration more accurate than it misses the p95 latency budget, and the one cheaper configuration that comes close, {arm:nano-xs.few}, fails the Complex × News floor. No interval is reported on any gate figure, so the open question is whether that thin overall clearance holds.
flag: No interval is reported on any gate figure: every pass and fail on this page reads a point estimate.

caveats.material_if: only if {arm:brisk-s.few}'s true balanced accuracy is below the overall gate: then no configuration passes every gate, and the choice becomes a trade between accuracy and the latency budget

only if the gold labels are noisy for medium complexity or Complex × News, where the errors and the binding cell sit; the gates are absolute lines, so label noise moves the readings against them, though it moves every configuration alike

decision.text: Serve the turn router on {arm:brisk-s.few}. It clears all three gates, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few} a month at current volume.
{arm:nano-xs.few} is cheaper and faster, but misses the Complex × News floor at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}.
{arm:brisk-s.rubric}, {arm:atlas-m.few} and {arm:atlas-m.rubric} are more accurate, but each misses the p95 budget of {criteria.p95.threshold}.
{arm:atlas-m.zero}, {arm:brisk-s.zero}, {arm:nano-xs.zero} and {arm:nano-xs.rubric} fall below the overall accuracy gate.

Overall accuracy is the weakest margin: {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points above the gate, with no interval, on the one configuration picked because it passed, which makes its estimate somewhat optimistic.
Complex × News is its weakest cell, {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|abs|pts} points above the floor, and the weakest cell for every configuration.
Compute case-level intervals for overall accuracy and the Complex × News cell on the frozen cases: if the overall interval crosses the gate, nothing passes robustly and the call becomes a trade.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} is the only one of {n_candidates|int} model and prompt configurations that passes all three gates.

evidence.caption: Each tile: balanced accuracy, cost, p95 latency and gate status, by model and prompt style; no interval is reported.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} clears the overall accuracy gate by {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points, the thinnest of its clearances.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy per configuration against the overall gate; points only, since no interval is reported.

claims.text: Complex × News is the weakest cell for every configuration: it keeps {arm:nano-xs.few} out at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, and {arm:brisk-s.few} clears it by {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|abs|pts} points.

evidence.caption: Accuracy in each cell for the two few-shot configurations a decider would weigh, with case counts; which label axis carries the Complex × News errors is not computed.

claims.text: Every configuration more accurate than {arm:brisk-s.few} misses the p95 latency budget.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy against p95 latency on a log axis, with the overall gate and the latency budget; Nano-XS few-shot sits inside both but fails a cell floor, which this chart does not draw.

claims.text: Rubric + reasoning lifts Atlas-M and Brisk-S but drops Nano-XS to {measure.balanced_accuracy.nano-xs.rubric.mean}, mostly by misreading medium complexity, so no prompt style's effect holds across models.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy by model, one bar per prompt style, drawn from zero with the overall gate; only Nano-XS falls from few-shot to rubric + reasoning.
Nano-XS complexity labels, few-shot against rubric + reasoning; rows are the true label, columns the predicted one.

explore.outcome: The call holds at any gate up to {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value}; above it, nothing passes.

explore.binds: every configuration's accuracy in each of the nine cells
explore.outcome: Below {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value} the call moves to {arm:nano-xs.few}; above {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.value}, nothing passes.

Below {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.value} nothing passes. A budget of {criteria.p95.atlas-m.few.value} or more admits more accurate, dearer configurations; the gates still pick {arm:brisk-s.few} on cost, but accuracy against cost would then be a trade nobody has priced.

omitted.why: Not gated, and they order the configurations near the decision the same way balanced accuracy does; full table only.
Domain errors are small for every configuration near the decision; complexity carries most errors, as the Nano-XS confusion shows.
Its errors are medium complexity read as a neighbour, symmetric on both sides; it describes the error shape and doesn't change the call.

omitted.what: Per-cell accuracy for the other seven configurations
omitted.why: Each is already out on a gate named in why-not; the full heatmap is in the appendix.
None lost or failed in any configuration; it describes the method.
The snapshot holds only p95 per configuration, so a p50-to-p95 range chart can't be drawn; p95 is what the gate reads.

omitted.what: A routed mix, such as sending Complex × News to Brisk-S and the rest to Nano-XS
omitted.why: This classifier produces the complexity and domain a router would route on, so the mix is circular as stated, and nobody ran it; no figure states its cost or accuracy.

next.text: Compute case-level intervals for overall balanced accuracy and for each cell's accuracy on the frozen cases.
next.settles: Whether {arm:brisk-s.few}'s overall and Complex × News clearances are clear of their lines; if the overall interval crosses the gate, nothing passes robustly and the call becomes a trade between accuracy and latency.

next.text: Confirm {arm:brisk-s.few} on a fresh sample of production turns.
next.settles: Whether the overall clearance survives outside the set it was picked on.

next.text: Add Complex × News examples to Nano-XS's few-shot prompt and re-run that configuration.
next.settles: Whether the cheapest near-passing option can clear the cell floor; it costs {cost_per_month.nano-xs.few} a month against {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few}, and its own overall clearance is only {criteria.overall.nano-xs.few.gap|abs|pts} points.

next.text: Run Brisk-S with the rubric but without the reasoning step.
next.settles: Whether the rubric's accuracy gain over few-shot fits inside the latency budget; today the rubric and the reasoning step change together, so neither can be credited.

next.text: Double-label a sample of medium-complexity and Complex × News turns.
next.settles: How much of the remaining error, and of the thin clearance, is label noise.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases|int} turns per configuration, the same turns for all {n_candidates|int}, spread over nine cells of complexity by domain; Complex × News holds {cells.complex.news.n_cases|int}. No repeats are recorded.
Three models crossed with three prompt styles: zero-shot, few-shot examples, and a rubric with a reasoning step. There is no control; all nine are new.

The share of turns whose predicted class matches the gold label. Balanced accuracy weights the classes equally; traffic-weighted accuracy weights them by traffic. The snapshot does not say whether a turn must match on both axes.

Balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold} overall; accuracy at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} in every cell; p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}. All were declared with the campaign; none was set after the results.
None reported on any figure. Every comparison reads point estimates.
Gold class labels; no annotator agreement figure is recorded.
Cost per turn, at {meta.volume_per_month|int} turns a month.
